column5: note

Queen sac (Qxh2+) starts a forced perpetual (Rh6+, Bh2+, Bg3+...); Maia-2600 rates the required follow-up Rh6+ only 28% raw / 31% post-truncation with no move-history conditioning, vs 56% for the losing Rxd1 line — verified project note 2026-07-10, confirmed not a sign bug.
column6: game 687537 ply 46 (chess.com import); FEN reconstructed via python-chess replay of the game PGN and cross-checked against `.planning/notes/2026-07-10-flawchess-engine-self-execution-analysis.md`, which independently matched the shipped Maia encoding to 0.01% against the UI (game not present in local dev DB; production DB access unavailable in this execution session, so the anchor position is taken from that already-published, independently-verified note rather than re-queried)

column5: The critical follow-up itself, one ply after the sac (after 24...Qxh2+ 25.Kxh2): Rh6+ is the only move that keeps the perpetual alive. This is exactly the node where Maia's lack of history planes bites — it has no way to know the queen sac two plies ago was the *point* of this rook lift.
column6: game 687537 ply 48 (chess.com import); same provenance as g687537-p46 above, one further ply of the verified PGN replay

column5: Non-capturing queen walk (Qh4-f2) into an attacked square whose point (a back-rank mating net) resolves 3 plies later; a history-blind policy has no signal that the queen offering itself for no immediate material gain is the winning idea.

column5: Queen sac (Qxh6) that only pays off via a kingside mating attack three plies later; a history-blind policy is prone to preferring a quieter developing or defensive move instead of surrendering the queen.

column5: Rook sac (Rxc6) that only wins via a Boden's-mate-style two-bishop net two moves later; giving up the exchange for a mating pattern is exactly the kind of delayed payoff a no-history policy underrates.

column5: Rook sac (Rxh7) starting a forced mating attack three plies later (attraction pattern — the king is dragged to h7); Maia lacks the history context that would explain why the rook is worth giving up here.
